visualReview.notes: Inspected all 11 current portable/source-terrain frames. St Giles has an open eight-rib stone crown with central shaft, four base pinnacles and tiered finial; its square tower has three narrow pointed louver fields per face. Broad lead-gray nave/choir, crossing, aisles and stepped side ranges retain the mapped massing. The west has a large pointed window above the wood entry, flanking pointed windows/blind niches, sparse tracery, buttress piers and northwest turret/cone. Three-window eastern choir and lower polygon-ended southeast Thistle Chapel remain distinct. Corrected the first estimated tower width/height against thirteen discovered map parts; connected tower/turret shafts down to their supporting mass, narrowed side-front niches, moved buttresses away from windows, cut overlapping walls and cleared roof-edge/cornice pieces across the upper east and west windows. The crown remains genuinely open; louver fields and doors/glass are closed. Exact carved figures, finial weathercock sculpture and stained-glass pictures are omitted.
